newsitem.title: JAPAN: U.S. Gulf-Japan grain freight rate falls.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Gulf-Japan grain freight rate falls.

text.p: The transpacific grain freight rate is showing a downward correction after gaining to around $26 a tonne last week, grain traders and shipping brokers said on Monday.
Nearby freight rates for the U.S. Gulf-Japan grain route were quoted at about $24 per tonne on Monday, the traders said.

"Chinese wheat imports and a temporary supply shortage of vessels in the U.S. helped support the freight to the $26 level by last week. But it is now showing a downward correction," a grain trader at a major trade house said.
The freight rate fell to $18.25 in September from about $23 in June, mainly because newly built Panamax-sized ships entered the market.

"The freight rate is unlikely to gain sharply from the current level. I think the rate will remain in a range of between $20 and $24 throughout this year," said Shingo Narumi, manager at Mitsui O.S.K. Lines Ltd's research department. -- Tokyo Commodity Desk +81-3-3432-7391
